Retrospective peels

Source: R/9-retro_and_jitter.R
retrospective.Rd

Calculate Mohn's rho and run retrospective peels for an Rceattle model, and evaluate retrospective forecast skill. Each peel uses TMB's map to:

  1. filter the data and fixed inputs and map out time-varying parameters for the peeled years, holding them at that peel's terminal year;

  2. fit the peeled model;

  3. turn the hindcast parameters off and F for the peeled years on, and fit to the peeled catch series, updating the "forecast" dynamics given the projection assumptions and the observed catch.

Usage

retrospective(
  object = NULL,
  peels = 5,
  rescale = FALSE,
  nyrs_forecast = 3,
  cores = NULL,
  getsd = NULL,
  phase = TRUE,
  fit_control = NULL,
  Rceattle = NULL
)

Arguments

object

an Rceattle model fit using fit_mod().

peels

number of retrospective peels used for rho and estimation

rescale

TRUE/FALSE whether to subset and rescale environmental predictors over the peel years.

nyrs_forecast

forecast years over which to calculate Mohn's rho, in addition to the terminal year

cores

Number of cores for the parallel refits. Default NULL picks parallel::detectCores() - 6, capped at 2 under R CMD check (which sets _R_CHECK_LIMIT_CORES_). Set to 1 to force sequential execution.

getsd

whether each peel reports standard errors through TMB::sdreport, at the cost of extra model builds (see Details); NULL (default) inherits the input model's setting (TRUE only if it holds an sdrep).

phase

whether each peel is refitted in phases, default TRUE. A peel restarts from the unpeeled fit's starting values with a year removed, so without phasing the parameters barely move, the peels sit on top of the full model, and Mohn's rho is biased toward zero. Change it only deliberately.

fit_control

optional fit_control() bundle for the refits. Only phase and getsd are read; see What fit_control() reaches.

Rceattle

deprecated name for object, still accepted so existing scripts keep working. Supplying both is an error.

Value

An Rceattle_retro list:

Rceattle_list

the unpeeled model and each kept peel, named for its own terminal year (Year_2017, ...). Index by name: the list runs from the deepest peel to the unpeeled model, and a dropped peel leaves a gap, so it can be shorter than peels + 1 and Rceattle_list[[3]] is not in general the 3-year peel. Each peel reports its terminal year as data_list$endyr, so plots draw it only as far as it was fit.

mohns

Mohn's rho by Object and Forecast year, one column per species, with N the number of peels averaged. With no peel left it is NaN, and the function warns.

peels_requested

the peels asked for.

A peel can carry attr(peel, "forecast_refit_error") or attr(peel, "sd_report_error"), each a one-line reason naming the peel and its terminal year (see Details); each is absent on every other peel.

Details

Each peel is fitted twice: a peeled hindcast, then a forecast refit estimating only the peeled years' F. The second holds every hindcast parameter fixed, so on its own it reports a standard error of zero across the hindcast. Under getsd = TRUE the peel is therefore rebuilt at those same parameters with the hindcast parameters treated as estimated and reported from there; nothing is re-estimated, so no point estimate moves.

A band in a fitted year is the peeled hindcast's own: the uncertainty of its parameters given the data through the peel's terminal year. The exception is a depletion that divides by last-projection-year biomass (HCR = "NoFishing" under msmMode > 0 and DynamicHCR = FALSE), which reads the peeled F, so its fitted-year bands move too. A band in a peeled (forecast) year treats that year's catch as known and its F as inferred from it: as the hindcast parameters vary, F moves, to first order, to keep the predicted catch at the observed catch, and the delta method carries that into the band. The peeled years' recruitment deviations are fixed at the projected deviation, so the band leaves out recruitment variability there and is narrower than a forecast's prediction interval.

Where that rebuild fails – it errors, its Hessian is not positive definite, it reports no finite standard error, or moving F with the hindcast parameters fails (its forecast years would then leave out F's response) – the peel keeps its point estimates, peel$sdrep keeps what TMB::sdreport() returned (NULL if the rebuild errored first; under an indefinite Hessian its numbers are not valid standard errors), and attr(peel, "sd_report_error") gives the reason, so plots, as.data.frame() and vcov() read none of it. print() counts such peels; no warning is raised, since the point estimates and Mohn's rho are unaffected.

Mohn's rho reads point estimates, so getsd = FALSE is faster, but TRUE also drops a peel whose hindcast Hessian is not positive definite, so the two can average over different peels.

A peel whose hindcast did not converge is dropped, with a warning. A peel whose forecast refit did not fit F to the peeled catch (gradient check, or a peeled F at a bound) is kept without a warning: its terminal-year Mohn's rho stands, but it is left out of the $mohns rows with Forecast year above 0 (N counts the peels used). Check attr(peel, "forecast_refit_error") before reading its forecast years or their standard errors; print() counts such peels, and plot_timeseries() and its wrappers warn when they draw those years.

A peel still estimates the years it dropped: that is its retrospective forecast, fit to observed catch with the survey and composition data withheld. Its recruitment deviation is the one sample_rec() sets with sample_rec = FALSE, computed from the peel's own fit. Three years matter, and every peel's data_list carries all three:

endyr, endyr_peel

the peel's terminal year, what it was fit through. Equal to each other.

endyr_full

the unpeeled model's terminal year, where the retrospective forecast ends.

projyr

the end of the harvest-control-rule projection.

Take the forecast years as endyr_peel + seq_len(endyr_full - endyr_peel), which is empty for the unpeeled model, rather than (endyr_peel + 1):endyr_full, which counts down there. Mohn's rho is computed from endyr_peel and is unaffected by any of this.

Catchability is estimated only for a fleet holding fitted index rows (see build_map), and a peel moves endyr, so a survey whose index observations all fall in the peeled-off years has no q estimated in that peel: the parameter count is not constant across peels. That is deliberate, since a q with no index to inform it is a flat direction in the likelihood. Rho is computed from SSB and is unaffected, but npar and the reported catchability do differ between a shallow and a deep peel for such a fleet.

Examples

# \donttest{
data(BS2017SS)
ss_run <- fit_mod(data_list = BS2017SS,
    inits = NULL, file = NULL,
    estimateMode = 0, random_rec = FALSE,
    msmMode = 0, avgnMode = 0,
    phase = FALSE, verbose = 0)
#> Warning: Passing ‘phase’, ‘verbose’ directly to fit_mod() is deprecated and will be removed in a future release. Bundle these into fit_control() instead, e.g. fit_control(phase = ..., verbose = ...). Forwarding for now.
#> `age_trans_matrix` data does not span range of age for species 1 will fill with 0s
retro <- retrospective(ss_run, peels = 10)
# }
